newsitem.title: ESTONIA: TALINVEST AIMS FOR 20 PCT OF BALTIC MARKET.
newsitem.headline: TALINVEST AIMS FOR 20 PCT OF BALTIC MARKET.

text.p: Talinvest's newly established investment firm TSB Securities hopes to gain a market share of 20-25 percent in three years, Peeter Saks, chairman of the board, said on Tuesday.
"The market is in the stage of formation and there are a lot of newcomers," Saks told Reuters in an interview.
The clients of the new Talinvest subsidiary will be formed by foreign as well as local investors, Saks said.
"The interest of foreign investors is different in the three states now but it is certainly going to level off as there is a trend for integration between the markets," Saks said.
In terms of turnover, foreign investors are more active in Estonia and Lithunia now, he added.
Saks named Hansapank's Hansa Investment as one of its competitors in terms of the pan-Baltic market.
"Hansa Investment is active in corporate finance, but not in trading," he added.
In the stock market area, Saks said Talinvest sees local commercial banks as its competitors.
TSB has a staff of 17 employees in Lithuania and 10 employees in Latvia, he added.
"The number in Estonia will be similar to Lithuania," Saks said.
Talinvest is integrating its present offices to the structure of the newly established investment firm, Saks added.
Talinvest has a majority stake in Lithuania's Suprema and has an office in Latvian capital Riga.
